title.zh: 卷一百四十七 列傳第三十五 解縉 黃淮 胡廣 金幼孜 胡儼
title.en: Volume 147 Biographies 35: Jie Jin, Huang Huai, Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, Hu Yan
title.raw: 卷一百四十七 列傳第三十五 解縉 黃淮 胡廣 金幼孜 胡儼 Volume 147 Biographies 35: Jie Jin, Huang Huai, Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, Hu Yan

sentences.zh: 解縉 黃淮 胡廣 金幼孜 胡儼

translations.literal: Jie Jin, Huang Huai, Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, Hu Yan
translations.idiomatic: Jie Jin, Huang Huai, Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, and Hu Yan

sentences.zh: 解縉，字大紳，吉水人。

translations.literal: Jie Jin, styled Dashen, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Jin, whose courtesy name was Dashen, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 祖子元，為元安福州判官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ziyuan served as prefectural judge of Yuan'an in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ziyuan had been the prefectural judge of Yuan'an in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 兵亂，守義死。

translations.literal: During the warfare he upheld righteousness and died.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out, he held to his duty and perished.

sentences.zh: 父開，太祖嘗召見論元事。

translations.literal: His father Kai—Taizu once summoned him to discuss Yuan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kai had once been summoned by the founding emperor to discuss affairs of the Yuan dynasty.

sentences.zh: 欲官之，辭去。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to give him an office; he declined and left.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint him, but he declined and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 縉幼穎敏，洪武二十一年舉進士。

translations.literal: Jin from youth was sharp and clever; in the twenty-first year of Hongwu he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Jin showed exceptional intelligence from childhood and passed the jinshi examinations in the twenty-first year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 授中書庶吉士，甚見愛重，常侍帝前。

translations.literal: He was appointed a junior compiler in the Central Secretariat, was greatly favored and esteemed, and often attended before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Made a junior compiler in the Central Secretariat, he won deep favor and was frequently at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝在大庖西室，諭縉：「朕與爾義則君臣，恩猶父子，當知無不言。」

translations.literal: One day the emperor, in the west chamber of the great kitchen, addressed Jin: "Between us in principle we are sovereign and minister, but in kindness we are like father and son—you ought to know there is nothing you should not speak."
translations.idiomatic: One day, while in the west chamber of the imperial kitchen, the emperor told Jin: "In title we are ruler and subject, but in affection we are like father and son—you must tell me everything.

sentences.zh: 縉即日上封事萬言，略曰：

translations.literal: That same day Jin submitted a sealed memorial of ten thousand characters, in summary saying:
translations.idiomatic: That same day Jin submitted a ten-thousand-character memorial that began:

sentences.zh: 臣聞令數改則民疑，刑太繁則民玩。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when orders are frequently changed the people become doubtful, and when punishments are too numerous the people become careless.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that if decrees change too often, the people lose confidence, and if punishments multiply, the people grow indifferent.

sentences.zh: 國初至今，將二十載，無幾時不變之法，無一日無過之人。

translations.literal: From the founding of the state until now, nearly twenty years—there has scarcely been a time without changing laws, scarcely a day without someone guilty of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the dynasty to the present, nearly twenty years have passed, yet scarcely a moment passes without some law being altered, scarcely a day without someone being found guilty of an offense.

sentences.zh: 嘗聞陛下震怒，鋤根剪蔓，誅其奸逆矣。

translations.literal: I have often heard Your Majesty in wrath uproot and cut away, executing traitors and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: I have often heard of Your Majesty's wrath uprooting whole clans and cutting off branches of kin, executing traitors and rebels.

sentences.zh: 未聞褒一大善，賞延於世，復及其鄉，終始如一者也。

translations.literal: I have not heard a single great good deed praised, reward extended through generations, reaching again to one's native place, consistent from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have not heard of a single great virtue rewarded, with honors extending through generations and reaching one's home district, maintained consistently from first to last.

sentences.zh: 臣見陛下好觀《說苑》、《韻府》雜書與所謂《道德經》、《心經》者，臣竊謂甚非所宜也。

translations.literal: Your subject sees Your Majesty fond of reading the Garden of Stories, the Rhyme Treasury, miscellaneous books, and the so-called Classic of the Way and of Virtue and Heart Sutra—I venture to say this is very inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Your Majesty enjoys reading the Garden of Stories, the Rhyme Treasury, miscellaneous compilations, and the so-called Daodejing and Heart Sutra—I must say this is most inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 《說苑》出於劉向，多戰國縱橫之論；

translations.literal: The Garden of Stories comes from Liu Xiang and contains much Warring States alliance-and-rivalry doctrine;
translations.idiomatic: The Garden of Stories was compiled by Liu Xiang and is full of Warring States strategems and diplomatic maneuvering;

sentences.zh: 《韻府》出元之陰氏，抄輯穢蕪，略無可採。

translations.literal: the Rhyme Treasury comes from the Yin family of the Yuan, copied and compiled in filthy confusion, scarcely anything worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: the Rhyme Treasury was compiled by the Yin family under the Yuan from plagiarized and worthless material, with scarcely anything worth reading.

sentences.zh: 陛下若喜其便於檢閱，則願集一二志士儒英，臣請得執筆隨其後，上溯唐、虞、夏、商、周、孔，下及關、閩、濂、洛。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty delights in their convenience for reference, then I wish to gather one or two men of resolve and eminent Confucians; your subject asks to take the brush and follow after them, tracing upward to Tang, Yu, Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Confucius, and downward to Guan, Min, Lian, and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty values their convenience for reference, I ask that one or two devoted scholars be assembled—I would take my brush and follow them, reaching back to the eras of Yao, Shun, Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Confucius, and forward to the traditions of Guanzi, the Min school, Lianxi, and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 根實精明，隨事類別，勒成一經，上接經史，豈非太平製作之一端歟？

translations.literal: With roots and fruits refined and clear, classifying matters as they arise, compel them into one classic linking upward to the classics and histories—would this not be one aspect of great peace's creative work?
translations.idiomatic: With substance made lucid and matters sorted by category, they could be compiled into a single classic linking upward to the canonical texts and histories—would this not be a worthy beginning to the literary achievements of an age of peace?

sentences.zh: 又今《六經》殘缺。

translations.literal: Moreover, today the Six Classics are incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Six Classics survive today only in damaged form.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》出於漢儒，踳駁尤甚，宜及時刪改。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites comes from Han Confucians and is especially contradictory and confused—it should promptly be edited and revised.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites was compiled by Han scholars and is especially riddled with inconsistencies—it should be revised without delay.

sentences.zh: 訪求審樂之儒，大備百王之典，作樂書一經以惠萬世。

translations.literal: Seek out Confucians versed in examining music, fully prepare the institutions of the hundred kings, and compose one classic on music to benefit ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Seek out scholars skilled in music theory, fully restore the ritual institutions of the ancient kings, and compile a classic on music that will benefit all posterity.

sentences.zh: 尊祀伏羲、神農、黃帝、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、皋陶、伊尹、太公、周公、稷、契、夷、益、傅說、箕子於太學。

translations.literal: Honor with sacrifice Fu Xi, Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Grand Duke, Duke of Zhou, Ji, Qi, Yi, Yi, Fu Yue, and Jizi in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Honor in the Imperial Academy with sacrificial rites Fu Xi, Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Jiang Ziya, the Duke of Zhou, Hou Ji, Qi, Bo Yi, Yi, Fu Yue, and Jizi.

sentences.zh: 孔子則自天子達於庶人，通祀以為先師，而以顏、曾、子思、孟子配。

translations.literal: Confucius then, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, should be universally sacrificed to as the foremost teacher, with Yan, Zeng, Zisi, and Mencius as associates.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius should be worshipped from the Son of Heaven down to the common people as the supreme teacher, with Yan Hui, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mencius as his correlates.

sentences.zh: 自閔子以下，各祭於其鄉。

translations.literal: From Minzi downward, each should be sacrificed to in his native district.
translations.idiomatic: From Min Sun downward, each disciple should receive sacrifices in his home district.

sentences.zh: 魯之闕里，仍建叔梁紇廟，贈以王爵，以顏路、曾曨、孔鯉配。

translations.literal: In Lu's Que li, still build a temple to Shuliang He, bestow the title of king, with Yan Lu, Zeng Dian, and Kong Li as associates.
translations.idiomatic: In Confucius's birthplace of Qufu, restore the temple to his father Shuliang He, grant him a royal title, and associate Yan Lu, Zeng Dian, and Kong Li with his cult.

sentences.zh: 一洗歷代之因仍，肇起天朝之文獻，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: Wash away at one stroke the inherited practices of successive dynasties, inaugurate the literary institutions of the heavenly dynasty—how would this not be magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: To sweep away at a stroke the accumulated customs of past dynasties and inaugurate the cultural institutions of our dynasty—what could be more glorious!

sentences.zh: 若夫祀天宜復掃地之規，尊祖宜備七廟之制。

translations.literal: As for sacrificing to Heaven, one should restore the rule of sweeping the ground; honoring ancestors, one should complete the institution of seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to Heaven should restore the ancient rite of preparing the ground by sweeping; honoring ancestors should restore the full institution of the seven ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 奉天不宜為筵宴之所，文淵未備夫館閣之隆。

translations.literal: Fengtian Hall should not serve as a place for banquets; the Hall of Literary Depth has not yet attained the grandeur of a pavilion and archive.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Imperial Supplication to Heaven should not be used for banquets, and the Hall of Literary Depth has not yet been endowed with the full dignity of a grand library.

sentences.zh: 太常非俗樂之可肄，官妓非人道之所為。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies is not a place where vulgar music may be practiced; official courtesans are not what human conduct permits.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices should not be a place for vulgar music, and official courtesans are not fitting for a civilized court.

sentences.zh: 禁絕倡優，易置寺閹。

translations.literal: Forbid entirely actors and entertainers; replace the eunuchs of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Ban actors and entertainers entirely, and replace the palace eunuchs with proper officials.

sentences.zh: 執戟陛墀，皆為吉士；

translations.literal: Those who hold halberds on the palace steps should all be men of excellence;
translations.idiomatic: The halberd-bearers on the palace steps should all be men of proven virtue;

sentences.zh: 虎賁趣馬，悉用俊良。

translations.literal: the Tiger Guards and outriders should all employ outstanding and good men.
translations.idiomatic: and the imperial guards and outriders should all be drawn from talented and upright men.

sentences.zh: 除山澤之禁稅，蠲務鎮之征商。

translations.literal: Remove prohibitory taxes on mountains and marshes; remit commercial levies at administrative posts.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish prohibitory taxes on mountains and marshes, and remit commercial levies at transit stations.

sentences.zh: 木輅樸居，而土木之工勿起；

translations.literal: Dwell in a plain wooden carriage and simple residence, and do not launch earth-and-wood construction projects;
translations.idiomatic: Live in plain wooden quarters, and do not launch grand construction projects;

sentences.zh: 布墾荒田，而四裔之地勿貪。

translations.literal: spread cultivation of waste land, but do not covet the territories of the four borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: encourage the reclamation of wasteland, but do not covet the territories beyond the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 釋、老之壯者驅之，俾復於人倫；

translations.literal: drive out the able-bodied among Buddhists and Daoists, causing them to return to human relations;
translations.idiomatic: Expel able-bodied Buddhist and Daoist monks, restoring them to ordinary family life;

sentences.zh: 經咒之妄者火之，俾絕其欺誑。

translations.literal: burn the false among sutras and incantations, causing deception to cease.
translations.idiomatic: and burn spurious scriptures and charms, putting an end to their fraud.

sentences.zh: 絕鬼巫，破淫祀，省冗官，減細縣。

translations.literal: Cut off ghost-worship and shamans, break licentious sacrifices, reduce redundant offices, diminish petty counties.
translations.idiomatic: Eliminate shamanism, abolish improper cults, reduce redundant offices, and consolidate petty counties.

sentences.zh: 痛懲法外之威刑，永革京城之工役。

translations.literal: Severely punish extra-legal coercive punishments; permanently abolish corvée labor in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Punish severely all punishments imposed outside the law, and permanently abolish forced labor in the capital.

sentences.zh: 流十年而聽復，杖八十以無加。

translations.literal: Exile for ten years then permit return; beating with the rod stops at eighty strokes with no addition.
translations.idiomatic: Permit exiles to return after ten years, and cap beating at eighty strokes with no additional punishment.

sentences.zh: 婦女非帷薄不修，毋令逮系；

translations.literal: Women who have not violated domestic propriety should not be seized and imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: Women who have not violated domestic propriety should not be arrested and imprisoned;

sentences.zh: 大臣有過惡當誅，不宜加辱。

translations.literal: When great ministers have faults and crimes deserving death, they should not be subjected to added humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers deserve execution for their crimes, they should not be subjected to additional humiliation.

sentences.zh: 治歷明時，授民作事，但申播植之宜，何用建除之謬。

translations.literal: Regulate the calendar to clarify the seasons, instruct the people in their work—only declare what is fitting for sowing and planting; why use the errors of the jianchu cycle?
translations.idiomatic: Regulate the calendar to clarify the seasons and instruct the people in their labors—declare only what is fitting for sowing and planting; why rely on the superstitious jianchu cycle?

sentences.zh: 所宜著者，日月之行，星辰之次。

translations.literal: What ought to be set forth are the courses of sun and moon, the positions of the stars.
translations.idiomatic: What ought to be recorded are the courses of the sun and moon and the positions of the stars.

sentences.zh: 仰觀俯察，事合逆順。

translations.literal: Observing above and examining below, affairs accord with what is adverse and what is favorable.
translations.idiomatic: Observing heaven above and earth below, affairs will accord with what is propitious and what is not.

sentences.zh: 七政之齊，正此類也。

translations.literal: The alignment of the seven regulators—this is precisely their kind.
translations.idiomatic: The proper alignment of the seven luminaries is precisely such a matter.

sentences.zh: 近年以來，台綱不肅。

translations.literal: In recent years the censorate's discipline has not been strict.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the censorate has lacked proper discipline.

sentences.zh: 以刑名輕重為能事，以問囚多寡為勛勞，甚非所以勵清要、長風采也。

translations.literal: Taking the severity of criminal names as their accomplishment, taking the number of prisoners interrogated as merit and labor—this is very far from what encourages purity and importance and fosters dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: They treat the severity of criminal charges as their achievement and the number of prisoners interrogated as their merit—this is no way to encourage integrity among the censorate or to uphold its dignity.

sentences.zh: 御史糾彈，皆承密旨。

translations.literal: Censors' impeachments all follow secret instructions.
translations.idiomatic: The censors' impeachments all follow secret instructions from above.

sentences.zh: 每聞上有赦宥，則必故為執持。

translations.literal: Whenever they hear that above there is an amnesty, they deliberately hold firm in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they hear that an amnesty has been proclaimed, they deliberately obstruct it.

sentences.zh: 意謂如此，則上恩愈重。

translations.literal: Their idea is that in this way the sovereign's grace becomes all the heavier.
translations.idiomatic: They imagine that by doing so the emperor's grace will appear all the greater.

sentences.zh: 此皆小人趨媚效勞之細術，陛下何不肝膽而鏡照之哉？

translations.literal: These are all petty techniques of petty men currying favor and rendering service—why does Your Majesty not lay bare your liver and gall and mirror-reflect upon them?
translations.idiomatic: These are all petty tricks of sycophants currying favor—why does Your Majesty not look upon them with complete openness and clarity?

sentences.zh: 陛下進人不擇賢否，授職不量重輕。

translations.literal: Your Majesty advances men without choosing whether they are worthy or not, assigns offices without measuring heavy or light.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty promotes men without regard to merit, and assigns offices without regard to their proper weight.

sentences.zh: 建不為君用之法，所謂取之盡錙銖；

translations.literal: You have established laws not for the sovereign's use—what is called taking to the last mite and grain;
translations.idiomatic: You have established laws that serve not the ruler but the tax collector—what is called extracting every last mite;

sentences.zh: 置朋奸倚法之條，所謂用之如泥沙。

translations.literal: you have set up provisions for factional villains who lean on the law—what is called using men like mud and sand.
translations.idiomatic: and provisions that allow corrupt associates to lean on the law—what is called using men like mud and sand.

sentences.zh: 監生進士，經明行修，而多屈於下僚；

translations.literal: Supervisory students and jinshi degree holders, classics clear and conduct cultivated, yet many are bent down to inferior offices;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial students and jinshi scholars, learned in the classics and upright in conduct, are often relegated to petty posts;

sentences.zh: 孝廉人材，冥蹈瞽趨，而或布於朝省。

translations.literal: filial and incorrupt candidates and human talent, blindly treading and groping in haste, yet some are spread through the court and ministries.
translations.idiomatic: while men recommended as filial and incorrupt, stumbling blindly forward, are sometimes placed in the central government.

sentences.zh: 椎埋嚚悍之夫，闒茸下愚之輩。

translations.literal: Men who bury and exhume, fierce and violent; the lowly and stupid, base and foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Violent ruffians and the lowest, most foolish sort of men.

sentences.zh: 朝捐刀鑷，暮擁冠裳。

translations.literal: In the morning they cast aside knife and tweezers; by evening they embrace cap and robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the morning they were barbers; by evening they wear official caps and robes.

sentences.zh: 左棄筐篋，右綰組符。

translations.literal: On the left they abandon baskets and boxes; on the right they tie on seals and tallies.
translations.idiomatic: They abandon their trade on the left and take up official seals on the right.

sentences.zh: 是故賢者羞為之等列，庸人悉習其風流。

translations.literal: Therefore the worthy are ashamed to be in the same rank with them; mediocrities all learn their ways and manners.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the worthy are ashamed to be ranked with them, while mediocrities all imitate their ways.

sentences.zh: 以貪婪苟免為得計，以廉潔受刑為飾辭。

translations.literal: They take greed and seeking escape as a winning plan; they take integrity and receiving punishment as ornamental words.
translations.idiomatic: They regard greed and evasion as shrewd policy, and integrity punished as mere pretense.

sentences.zh: 出於吏部者無賢否之分，入於刑部者無枉直之判。

translations.literal: Those who come out of the Ministry of Personnel have no distinction of worthy or not; those who enter the Ministry of Punishments have no judgment of crooked or straight.
translations.idiomatic: Those who leave the Ministry of Personnel are promoted without regard to merit, and those who enter the Ministry of Punishments are judged without regard to justice.

sentences.zh: 天下皆謂陛下任喜怒為生殺，而不知皆臣下之乏忠良也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven say Your Majesty lets joy and anger decide life and death, and do not know it is all because your subjects below lack loyal worthies.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven believe Your Majesty lets whim decide life and death, not knowing that it is because your ministers lack loyal and worthy men.

sentences.zh: 古者善惡，鄉鄰必記。

translations.literal: In antiquity good and evil—neighbors in the district certainly recorded them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, good and evil deeds were always recorded by one's neighbors.

sentences.zh: 今雖有申明旌善之舉，而無黨庠鄉學之規。

translations.literal: Today although there is the practice of declaring and honoring goodness, there are no regulations for district schools and village academies.
translations.idiomatic: Today, although there are measures to proclaim and honor virtue, there are no regulations for district schools and village academies.

sentences.zh: 互知之法雖嚴，訓告之方未備。

translations.literal: Though the mutual surveillance law is strict, methods of instruction and admonition are not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Though the law of mutual surveillance is strict, methods of instruction and admonition are not yet in place.

sentences.zh: 臣欲求古人治家之禮，睦鄰之法，若古藍田呂氏之《鄉約》，今義門鄭氏之家范，布之天下。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to seek the ancients' rites for governing the family and methods for harmonizing neighbors, like the ancient Lantian Lü clan's Village Compact and the present Righteous Gate Zheng clan's family standards, and spread them through all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ancients' rules for household governance and neighborly harmony—such as the Lü clan's Village Compact of Lantian and the Zheng clan's family standards of the Righteous Gate—be promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 世臣大族，率先以勸，旌之復之，為民表帥。

translations.literal: Hereditary ministers and great clans should take the lead in encouragement; honor them and restore them, making them models for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary ministers and great clans should take the lead in this effort; honor and restore them, making them models for the people.

sentences.zh: 將見作新於變，至於比屋可封不難矣。

translations.literal: We shall see renewal through transformation, until every household may be enfeoffed—not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: We shall see renewal through transformation, until every household in the realm may be deemed worthy of honor—not a difficult goal.

sentences.zh: 陛下天資至高，合於道微。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heavenly endowment is supremely high, in accord with the subtlety of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's natural gifts are supreme, in harmony with the subtle Way.

sentences.zh: 神怪妄誕，臣知陛下洞矚之矣。

translations.literal: Spirits and monsters, wild and absurd—your subject knows Your Majesty sees through them clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits and monsters, wild and absurd—I know Your Majesty sees through them clearly.

sentences.zh: 然猶不免所謂神道設教者，臣謂不必然也。

translations.literal: Yet you still cannot avoid what is called establishing teaching through the divine way—I say it is not necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still resort to what is called establishing teaching through the divine way—I say this is not necessary.

sentences.zh: 一統之輿圖已定矣，一時之人心已服矣，一切之奸雄已慴矣。

translations.literal: The cartographic map of unified rule is already fixed; the hearts of the people for a time are already submissive; all villainous strongmen are already cowed.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is already unified, the people's hearts are already won, and all rival strongmen are already subdued.

sentences.zh: 天無變災，民無患害。

translations.literal: Heaven has no strange disasters; the people have no calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends no strange disasters, and the people suffer no calamities.

sentences.zh: 聖躬康寧，聖子聖孫繼繼繩繩。

translations.literal: The sage person is healthy and at peace; sage sons and sage grandsons continue in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Your sacred person enjoys health and peace, and sage sons and grandsons succeed one another in unbroken line.

sentences.zh: 所謂得真符者矣。

translations.literal: This is what is called obtaining the true mandate.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to hold the true Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 何必興師以取寶為名，諭眾以神仙為征應也哉。

translations.literal: Why must you raise armies in the name of seeking treasures, instruct the multitude with immortals and spirits as signs and responses?
translations.idiomatic: Why must you raise armies in the name of seeking treasures, or tell the people that immortals and spirits are the signs of Heaven's favor?

sentences.zh: 臣觀地有盛衰，物有盈虛，而商稅之征，率皆定額。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that land has flourishing and decline, things have fullness and emptiness, yet commercial tax levies are mostly fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that land has its seasons of fertility and decline, and goods their cycles of abundance and scarcity, yet commercial taxes are mostly fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 是使其或盈也，奸黠得以侵欺；

translations.literal: This causes that when there is abundance, the crafty and cunning can encroach and cheat;
translations.idiomatic: When times are prosperous, the crafty can evade payment;

sentences.zh: 其歉也，良善困於補納。

translations.literal: when there is scarcity, the good and honest are trapped in making up payments.
translations.idiomatic: when times are lean, the honest are burdened with making up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 夏稅一也，而茶椒有糧，果絲有稅。

translations.literal: Summer tax is one, yet tea and pepper have grain levies, fruit and silk have taxes.
translations.idiomatic: There is but one summer tax, yet tea and pepper bear grain levies, and fruit and silk bear separate taxes.

sentences.zh: 既稅於所產之地，又稅於所過之津，何其奪民之利至於如此之密也！

translations.literal: Taxed both at the place of production and again at the ferry crossings passed—how is seizing the people's profit carried to such density!
translations.idiomatic: Taxed at the place of production and again at every ferry crossing—how can the people's profit be seized so relentlessly!

sentences.zh: 且多貧下之家，不免拋荒之咎。

translations.literal: Moreover many poor and lowly households cannot escape the blame of abandoning fields to waste.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, many poor households cannot escape blame for letting their fields lie fallow.

sentences.zh: 今日之土地，無前日之生植；

translations.literal: Today's land lacks yesterday's growth and planting;
translations.idiomatic: Today's land no longer yields what it once did;

sentences.zh: 而今日之征聚，有前日之稅糧。

translations.literal: yet today's collections and levies have yesterday's tax grain.
translations.idiomatic: yet today's levies still demand yesterday's tax quotas.

sentences.zh: 或賣產以供稅，產去而稅存；

translations.literal: Some sell property to supply taxes—the property goes but the tax remains;
translations.idiomatic: Some sell their property to pay taxes—the property is gone but the tax remains;

sentences.zh: 或賠辦以當役，役重而民困。

translations.literal: some compensate and fulfill to substitute for corvée—the corvée is heavy and the people are distressed.
translations.idiomatic: some pay substitutes for corvée labor—the burdens are heavy and the people are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 土田之高下不均，起科之輕重無別。

translations.literal: Fields' high and low are not equal; initiating assessment makes no distinction of light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Fields vary in quality, yet tax assessments make no distinction between fertile and poor land.

sentences.zh: 膏腴而稅反輕，瘠鹵而稅反重。

translations.literal: Rich and fertile land yet tax conversely light; barren and saline yet tax conversely heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Fertile land is taxed lightly, while barren saline soil is taxed heavily.

sentences.zh: 欲拯困而革其弊，莫若行授田均田之法，兼行常平義倉之舉。

translations.literal: To save distress and reform these abuses, nothing is better than implementing the methods of granting fields and equalizing fields, together with the practice of ever-normal and righteous granaries.
translations.idiomatic: To relieve distress and reform these abuses, nothing would be better than implementing land distribution and equal-field systems, together with ever-normal granaries and community relief stores.

sentences.zh: 積之以漸，至有九年之食無難者。

translations.literal: Accumulate by degrees, until having nine years' food is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulate grain gradually, until a nine-year reserve is easily within reach.

sentences.zh: 臣聞仲尼曰：「王公設險以守其國。」

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Zhongni said: "Kings and dukes establish defenses to guard their states."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard Confucius say: "Kings and lords establish defenses to guard their states.

sentences.zh: 近世狃於晏安，墮名城，銷鋒鏑，禁兵諱武，以為太平。

translations.literal: In recent generations accustomed to ease and comfort, famous cities have been destroyed, sharp points and arrowheads melted down, troops forbidden and martial affairs tabooed, taking this for great peace.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times, accustomed to ease and comfort, famous cities have been dismantled, weapons melted down, and military training forbidden—all in the name of peace.

sentences.zh: 一旦有不測之虞，連城望風而靡。

translations.literal: Once there is unforeseen apprehension, linked cities gaze at the wind and crumble.
translations.idiomatic: Once unforeseen danger arises, whole chains of cities will collapse at the first rumor.

sentences.zh: 及今宜敕有司整葺，寬之以歲月，守之以里胥，額設弓手，兼教民兵。

translations.literal: By now Your Majesty should order the responsible offices to repair and restore, allow time in years and months, guard through village officers, set quotas for archers, and also teach militia.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should now order the responsible offices to repair the defenses, allow adequate time, assign village officers to maintain them, establish quotas for archers, and train local militia.

sentences.zh: 開武舉以收天下之英雄，廣鄉校以延天下之俊乂。

translations.literal: Open military examinations to gather the empire's heroes; broaden village schools to extend the empire's outstanding talents.
translations.idiomatic: Establish military examinations to recruit the empire's heroes, and expand village schools to draw in the empire's finest talents.

sentences.zh: 古時多有書院學田，貢士有庄，義田有族，皆宜興復而廣益之。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were many academy school fields; tribute scholars had estates, righteous fields had clans—all should be revived and broadly increased.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there were many academy lands, estates for examination candidates, and clan charity fields—all should be revived and expanded.

sentences.zh: 夫罪人不孥，罰弗及嗣。

translations.literal: Now, punishment does not extend to the criminal's family, and penalties do not reach his heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment should not extend to the criminal's family, nor penalties to his heirs.

sentences.zh: 連坐起於秦法，孥戮本於偽書。

translations.literal: Collective punishment arose from Qin law; execution of the criminal together with his family originates from spurious texts.
translations.idiomatic: Collective punishment began with Qin law, and the slaughter of a criminal's entire family rests on forged texts.

sentences.zh: 今之為善者妻子未必蒙榮，有過者里胥必陷其罪。

translations.literal: Now among those who do good, wives and children do not necessarily receive honor; among those who have faults, village officers must trap them in guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Today those who do good cannot be sure their families will be rewarded, while anyone who errs is sure to be framed by local officials.

sentences.zh: 況律以人倫為重，而有給配婦女之條，聽之於不義，則又何取夫節義哉。

translations.literal: Moreover, since law takes human relations as weighty, yet there are provisions for assigning women in marriage—if one listens to what is unrighteous, then what is taken from chastity and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the law should uphold human relations, how can we countenance provisions for forcibly marrying off women? To condone such injustice is to abandon all regard for chastity and moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 此風化之所由也。

translations.literal: This is what customs and moral transformation arise from.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what undermines social morals.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「名不正則言不順。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "If names are not correct, then words are not in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "When names are improper, speech cannot be coherent.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎，內侍也，而以加於六卿；

translations.literal: Minister and Vice Minister were inner attendants, yet they are applied upon the six chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Minister and Vice Minister were titles for inner court attendants, yet they have been applied to the six chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外，內職也，而以名於六屬。

translations.literal: Bureau Director and Outside Director were inner offices, yet they are used as names for the six ministries' subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director and Outside Director were inner court posts, yet they now serve as titles for the six ministries' subordinates.

sentences.zh: 御史詞臣，所以居寵台閣；

translations.literal: Censors and literary officials are what occupy favored positions in the halls of state;
translations.idiomatic: Censors and literary officials were meant to hold honored positions in the halls of state;

sentences.zh: 郡守縣令，不應迴避鄉邦。

translations.literal: Prefects and county magistrates should not avoid their home regions.
translations.idiomatic: yet prefects and magistrates ought not be barred from serving in their own home districts.

sentences.zh: 同寅協恭，相倡以禮。

translations.literal: Colleagues of the same year assist one another with respect, mutually leading by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues should assist one another with mutual respect and encourage one another through proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 而今內外百司捶楚屬官，甚於奴隸。

translations.literal: Yet now within and without, the hundred offices beat and thrash their subordinate officials, worse than slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today government offices at every level beat and torture their subordinates worse than slaves.

sentences.zh: 是使柔懦之徒，盪無廉恥，進退奔趨，肌膚不保。

translations.literal: This causes the soft and timid sort to be swept clean of integrity and shame, advancing and retreating in frantic haste, their flesh and skin not preserved.
translations.idiomatic: This reduces the weak and timid to abject shamelessness—they scurry about in fear, their bodies broken and bleeding.

sentences.zh: 甚非所以長孝行、勵節義也。

translations.literal: It is very much not the way to foster filial conduct and encourage integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Far from nurturing filial piety and moral courage, this destroys them.

sentences.zh: 臣以為自今非犯罪惡解官，笞杖之刑勿用。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that from now on, except for commission of wicked crimes warranting dismissal from office, the punishment of beating with the rod should not be used.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that henceforth, except for dismissal on grounds of serious crime, the flogging punishments should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 催科督厲，小有過差，蒲鞭示辱，亦足懲矣。

translations.literal: In collecting taxes and supervising enforcement, for slight faults and errors, a reed whip to show humiliation is also sufficient as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In tax collection and routine supervision, minor lapses might be corrected with nothing more than a symbolic stroke of the reed whip.

sentences.zh: 臣但知罄竭愚衷，急於陳獻，略無次序，惟陛下幸垂鑒焉。

translations.literal: Your subject only knows to exhaust his foolish sincerity, urgent in presenting and offering, slightly without order, only wishing Your Majesty would graciously look down and examine.
translations.idiomatic: I have poured out my humble thoughts in haste, without proper order; I can only hope Your Majesty will deign to consider them.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝稱其才。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; the Emperor praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 已，復獻《太平十策》，文多不錄。

translations.literal: Afterward, he again presented "Ten Policies for Great Peace"; the text is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted his "Ten Policies for Great Peace," but most of the text is not preserved here.

sentences.zh: 縉嘗入兵部索皁隸，語嫚。

translations.literal: Jin once entered the Ministry of War to demand menial clerks, his speech rude.
translations.idiomatic: Jin once went to the Ministry of War to demand office runners and spoke insolently.

sentences.zh: 尚書沈溍以聞。

translations.literal: Minister Shen Wen reported it to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Shen Wen reported the matter to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「縉以冗散自恣耶。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Is Jin indulging himself because he holds a supernumerary post?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Does Jin think his idle appointment entitles him to behave so freely?

sentences.zh: 命改為御史。

translations.literal: He ordered that Jin be changed to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that Jin be transferred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 韓國公李善長得罪死，縉代郎中王國用草疏白其冤。

translations.literal: The Duke of Han, Li Shanchang, offended and died; Jin on behalf of Bureau Director Wang Guoyong drafted a memorial to proclaim his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: After the Duke of Han, Li Shanchang, was condemned and executed, Jin drafted a memorial on behalf of Bureau Director Wang Guoyong to plead Li's innocence.

sentences.zh: 又為同官夏長文草疏，劾都御史袁泰。

translations.literal: Again he drafted a memorial for his fellow official Xia Changwen, impeaching Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted a memorial for his colleague Xia Changwen impeaching Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰深銜之。

translations.literal: Tai deeply harbored resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tai came to hate him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時近臣父皆得入覲。

translations.literal: At that time the fathers of favored officials could all enter to have audience.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the fathers of favored officials were permitted to come to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 縉父開至，帝謂曰：「大器晚成，若以而子歸，益令進學，後十年來，大用未晚也。」

translations.literal: Jin's father Kai arrived; the Emperor said to him: "Great vessels mature late—if you take your son home, further order him to advance in learning; after ten years when he comes, great appointment is not too late.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's father, Kai, arrived, the Emperor told him, "Great talent ripens slowly. Take your son home and see that he continues his studies. Even if he returns ten years from now, it will not be too late to give him important responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 歸八年，太祖崩，縉入臨京師。

translations.literal: After eight years at home, Emperor Taizu died; Jin entered the capital to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later, when Emperor Taizu died, Jin came to the capital to mourn.

sentences.zh: 有司劾縉違詔旨，且母喪未葬，父年九十，不當舍以行。

translations.literal: The relevant officials impeached Jin for violating the imperial edict, moreover his mother's funeral had not been conducted, his father was ninety years old—he should not have abandoned them to go.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached him for defying the Emperor's orders—they noted that his mother had not yet been buried and his father was ninety years old, and that he should not have left home.

sentences.zh: 謫河州衛吏。

translations.literal: He was demoted to clerk of Hezhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to serve as a clerk in Hezhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 時禮部侍郎董倫方為惠帝所信任，縉因寓書於倫曰：「縉率易狂愚，無所避忌，數上封事，所言分封勢重，萬一不幸，必有厲長、吳濞之虞。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of Rites Dong Lun was just then trusted by Emperor Huidi; Jin therefore sent a letter to Dong Lun saying: "I, Jin, am careless, reckless and foolish, without avoidance or taboo; I have repeatedly submitted sealed memorials, speaking of how the enfeoffed princes' power is weighty—if by chance misfortune occurs, there will surely be the apprehension of Liu Chang and Wu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Minister of Rites Dong Lun enjoyed the trust of Emperor Huidi, and Jin sent him a letter saying, "I am rash, reckless, and foolish, and speak without restraint. In my repeated sealed memorials I warned that the enfeoffed princes had grown too powerful—that if misfortune should strike, the realm would face rebellions like those of Liu Chang and Wu Pi.

sentences.zh: 冉阝哈術來歸，欽承顧問，謂宜待之有禮，稍忤機權，其徒必貳。

translations.literal: When Lan Yu came to surrender, honored to receive His Majesty's consultation, one should treat him with courtesy; slightly go against imperial authority, his followers will surely turn disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Yu came over in submission and was honored with the Emperor's attention, I urged that he be treated with courtesy—a slight offense to imperial authority, I warned, and his followers would turn traitorous.

sentences.zh: 此類非一，頗皆億中。

translations.literal: Matters of this sort were not one; many all hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: I made many such predictions, most of which proved accurate.

sentences.zh: 又嘗為王國用草諫書，言韓國事，為詹徽所疾，欲中以危法。

translations.literal: Again he once drafted a remonstrance for Wang Guoyong, speaking of the Han ducal affair; he was resented by Zhan Hui, who wished to trap him with severe law.
translations.idiomatic: I also once drafted a remonstrance for Wang Guoyong on the case of the Duke of Han, for which Zhan Hui bore me ill will and sought to trap me with capital charges.

sentences.zh: 伏蒙聖恩，申之慰諭，重以鏹賜，令以十年著述，冠帶來廷。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I received sacred grace; it was extended in consolation and instruction, additionally with silver granted, ordering me to spend ten years in writing, then come to court wearing official cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: I was spared by Your Majesty's grace, consoled and reassured, and granted silver besides, with orders to spend ten years in scholarly work before returning to court in official dress.

sentences.zh: 《元史》舛誤，承命改修，及踵成《宋書》，刪定《禮經》，凡例皆已留中。

translations.literal: The History of Yuan had errors; I received orders to revise it, and subsequently completed the History of Song, edited and fixed the Classic of Rites—all guidelines have already been kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to revise the flawed History of Yuan, went on to complete the History of Song, and edited the Classic of Rites—all of whose guidelines have already been submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 奉親之暇，杜門纂述，漸有次第，洊將八載。

translations.literal: In spare time while serving my parents, I closed my door to compile and write; gradually there was order, nearly reaching eight years.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals of caring for my parents, I shut my door to write, and my work had steadily progressed for nearly eight years.

sentences.zh: 賓天之訃忽聞，痛切欲絕。

translations.literal: News of the Emperor's ascent to heaven was suddenly heard; grief cut to the point of wanting to perish.
translations.idiomatic: When sudden word came of the Emperor's death, my grief was unbearable.

sentences.zh: 母喪在殯，未遑安厝。

translations.literal: My mother's funeral lay in the coffin; there was no leisure to lay her to rest.
translations.idiomatic: My mother's coffin had not yet been buried.

sentences.zh: 家有九十之親，倚門望思，皆不暇戀。

translations.literal: At home was a relative of ninety years, leaning on the door gazing in longing—all without leisure to cherish.
translations.idiomatic: At home my ninety-year-old father waited at the door, longing for my return, yet I had no time even to linger with him.

sentences.zh: 冀一拜山陵，隕淚九土。

translations.literal: I hoped to bow once at the imperial tomb and shed tears upon the nine regions of earth.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped only to pay one visit to the imperial tomb and weep upon the earth.

sentences.zh: 何圖詿誤，蒙恩遠行。

translations.literal: Who would have thought I would fall into error and, receiving grace, be sent on a distant journey.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, through some misunderstanding, I have been sent far from home.

sentences.zh: 揚、粵之人，不耐寒暑，復多疾病。

translations.literal: People of Yang and Yue cannot endure cold and heat, and moreover suffer many illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: A man of the Yangzi and Guangdong regions, I cannot endure the extremes of climate there, and I am often ill.

sentences.zh: 俯仰奔趨，伍於吏卒，誠不堪忍。

translations.literal: Bowing and rushing about, ranked with clerks and soldiers—it is truly unbearable to endure.
translations.idiomatic: I must bow and scurry about among clerks and soldiers—a humiliation I truly cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 晝夜涕泣，恆懼不測。

translations.literal: Day and night I weep tears, constantly fearing the unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: I weep day and night, living in constant dread of what may befall me.

sentences.zh: 負平生之心，抱萬古之痛。

translations.literal: I bear against the heart of a lifetime and embrace pain of ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: I have betrayed the ideals of a lifetime and carry a grief that will never fade.

sentences.zh: 是以數鳴知感。

translations.literal: Therefore I repeatedly cry out to make my feelings known.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I appeal again and again to make my plight known.

sentences.zh: 冀還京師，得望天顏，或遂南還，父子相見，即更生之日也。」

translations.literal: I hope to return to the capital, obtain sight of the imperial countenance, or then go south and return, father and son meeting—that would be the day of rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: If I might return to the capital and behold the Emperor's face, or go home to the south and see my father again, it would be as if I were born anew.

sentences.zh: 倫乃薦縉，召為翰林待詔。

translations.literal: Dong Lun then recommended Jin, and he was summoned as Hanlin Awaiting Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Lun thereupon recommended Jin, and he was recalled to serve as a Hanlin awaiting-edicts.

sentences.zh: 成祖入京師，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: When Chengzu entered the capital, Jin was promoted to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor entered the capital, Jin was promoted to Reader.

sentences.zh: 命與黃淮、楊士奇、胡廣、金幼孜、楊榮、胡儼並直文淵閣，預機務。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Huang Huai, Yang Shiqi, Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, Yang Rong, and Hu Yan jointly to attend at the Pavilion of Literary Depths and participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve alongside Huang Huai, Yang Shiqi, Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, Yang Rong, and Hu Yan in the Pavilion of Literary Depths, participating in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 內閣預機務自此始。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat's participation in state affairs began from this.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the beginning of the Grand Secretariat's role in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋進侍讀學士，奉命總裁《太祖實錄》及《列女傳》。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Reader and Academician, ordered to serve as chief editor of the Veritable Records of Taizu and the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Reader and Academician and ordered to serve as chief editor of the Veritable Records of Taizu and the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 書成，賜銀幣。

translations.literal: When the books were completed, silver and silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the works were completed, he was rewarded with silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，皇太子立，進縉翰林學士兼右春坊大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle, the Crown Prince was established; Jin was advanced to Hanlin Academician and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Right Chunfang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongle reign, when the Crown Prince was installed, Jin was promoted to Hanlin Academician and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Right Chunfang.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗召縉等曰：「爾七人朝夕左右，朕嘉爾勤慎，時言之宮中。

translations.literal: The Emperor once summoned Jin and the others, saying: "You seven are morning and evening at My side; I commend your diligence and care, and often speak of you within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once summoned Jin and the others and said, "You seven attend me day and night. I commend your diligence and discretion, and often speak of you within the palace.

sentences.zh: 恆情，慎初易，保終難，願共勉焉。」

translations.literal: Ordinary feeling: being careful at the start is easy, preserving to the end is hard—I wish we may encourage one another in this.
translations.idiomatic: It is human nature to begin with care but hard to persevere to the end. Let us encourage one another in this.

sentences.zh: 因各賜五品服，命七人命婦朝皇后於柔儀殿，後勞賜備至。

translations.literal: Thereupon each was granted fifth-rank robes; the seven men's wives were ordered to attend upon the Empress at Ruyi Hall, and the Empress rewarded them with full generosity.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted each of them fifth-rank robes and ordered their wives to attend upon the Empress at Ruyi Hall, where the Empress received them with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 又以立春日賜縉等金綺衣，與尚書埒。

translations.literal: Again on the Start of Spring day he granted Jin and the others brocade robes, equal to Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On the Start of Spring he also granted Jin and the others brocade robes equal to those worn by ministers.

sentences.zh: 縉等入謝，帝曰：「代言之司，機密所系，且旦夕侍朕，裨益不在尚書下也。」

translations.literal: Jin and the others entered to give thanks; the Emperor said: "The office of drafting words is where confidential matters depend; moreover morning and evening you attend on Me—your benefit is not below Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin and the others came to give thanks, the Emperor said, "Your office drafts the imperial word and handles state secrets. You attend me day and night, and your service is no less valuable than that of any minister.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝御奉天門，諭六科諸臣直言，因顧縉等曰：「王、魏之風，世不多有。

translations.literal: One day the Emperor took the throne at Fengtian Gate, instructing the officials of the Six Offices to speak frankly; turning to Jin and the others he said: "The spirit of Wang and Wei, the world does not have many.
translations.idiomatic: One day, holding court at Fengtian Gate, the Emperor urged the Six Offices to speak frankly, then turned to Jin and the others and said, "The forthright spirit of Wang Ji and Wei Zheng is rare in any age.

sentences.zh: 若使進言者無所懼，聽言者無所忤，天下何患不治？

translations.literal: If those who advance words have nothing to fear, and those who listen have nothing to take offense at, what worry is there that the realm will not be governed?
translations.idiomatic: If those who speak up need fear nothing and those who listen take no offense, what obstacle could stand in the way of good government?

sentences.zh: 朕與爾等共勉之。」

translations.literal: I with you all will encourage one another in this."
translations.idiomatic: Let us all strive together toward that end."

sentences.zh: 其年秋，胡儼出為祭酒，縉等六人從容獻納。

translations.literal: That autumn Hu Yan went out as Libationer; Jin and the other six at leisure presented and accepted advice.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Hu Yan left to serve as Libationer, and Jin and the remaining six continued to offer counsel at their ease.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗虛己以聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor often emptied himself to listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often listened with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 縉少登朝，才高，任事直前，表裏洞達。

translations.literal: Jin entered court young; his talent was high, he undertook affairs straight ahead, inside and outside transparent.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had entered government young. Highly talented, he tackled affairs head-on and was transparent in all he did.

sentences.zh: 引拔士類，有一善稱之不容口。

translations.literal: He promoted scholar-officials; for one good point he praised them without stopping his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted men of talent and never ceased praising anyone who showed the slightest merit.

sentences.zh: 然好臧否，無顧忌，廷臣多害其寵。

translations.literal: Yet he liked to pass judgment on good and bad, without regard or fear; court ministers many resented his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was quick to pass judgment on others and spoke without restraint, and many court officials resented his favored position.

sentences.zh: 又以定儲議，為漢王高煦所忌，遂致敗。

translations.literal: Also because of fixing the heir discussion, he was envied by the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, and thus led to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He also earned the enmity of the Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, by his role in settling the succession, and this ultimately brought about his downfall.

sentences.zh: 先是，儲位未定，淇國公邱福言漢王有功，宜立。

translations.literal: Before this, the heir's position was not fixed; Duke of Qi Qiu Fu said the Prince of Han had merit and should be established.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the succession had not been settled, the Duke of Qi, Qiu Fu, argued that the Prince of Han had earned merit and ought to be made heir.

sentences.zh: 帝密問縉。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly asked Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor privately asked Jin's opinion.

sentences.zh: 縉稱：「皇長子仁孝，天下歸心。」

translations.literal: Jin said: "The eldest imperial son is benevolent and filial; the realm turns its heart to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin replied, "The eldest imperial son is benevolent and filial, and the hearts of the realm are with him.

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 縉又頓首曰：「好聖孫。」

translations.literal: Jin again bowed his head and said: "A good holy grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kowtowed again and said, "And what a fine imperial grandson he has.

sentences.zh: 謂宣宗也。

translations.literal: He meant the Xuanzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was referring to the future Xuanzong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 太子遂定。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was thus fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's position was thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 高煦由是深恨縉。

translations.literal: Gaoxu from this deeply hated Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxu henceforth hated Jin deeply.

sentences.zh: 會大發兵討安南，縉諫。

translations.literal: When great troops were raised to attack Annam, Jin remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When a major campaign was launched against Annam, Jin remonstrated against it.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 卒平之，置郡縣。

translations.literal: Finally it was pacified, and prefectures and counties were established.
translations.idiomatic: Annam was eventually pacified and organized into prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 而太子既立，又時時失帝意。

translations.literal: Yet though the Crown Prince had been established, he also from time to time lost the Emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even after the Crown Prince was installed, he often fell out of the Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 高煦寵益隆，禮秩逾嫡。

translations.literal: Gaoxu's favor grew ever more elevated; ritual rank exceeded the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxu's favor only grew, and his ceremonial rank surpassed that of the heir.

sentences.zh: 縉又諫曰：「是啟爭也，不可。」

translations.literal: Jin again remonstrated, saying: "This opens contention—it cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Jin remonstrated again, saying, "This invites rivalry—it must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謂其離間骨肉，恩禮浸衰。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, saying he was sowing discord between kin; grace and ritual gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angry, accusing him of sowing discord within the imperial family, and Jin's favor steadily waned.

sentences.zh: 四年，賜黃淮等五人二品紗羅衣，而不及縉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Huang Huai and five others were granted second-rank gauze silk robes, but it did not reach Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Huang Huai and five others were granted second-rank gauze robes, but Jin was excluded.

sentences.zh: 久之，福等議稍稍傳達外廷，高煦遂譖縉泄禁中語。

translations.literal: After a long time, Fu and others' discussion gradually spread to the outer court; Gaoxu then slandered Jin for leaking forbidden palace words.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Qiu Fu's proposal began to circulate outside the palace, and Gaoxu then accused Jin of leaking confidential discussions.

sentences.zh: 明年，縉坐廷試讀卷不公，謫廣西布政司參議。

translations.literal: The next year, Jin was convicted for unfair reading of palace examination papers and was demoted to Administrative Commissioner Assistant of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jin was convicted of bias in grading the palace examinations and was demoted to Administrative Commissioner Assistant in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 既行，禮部郎中李至剛言縉怨望，改交阯，命督餉化州。

translations.literal: After he had departed, Libationer Li Zhigang of the Ministry of Rites said Jin was resentful; his assignment was changed to Jiaozhi, and he was ordered to supervise provisions at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After he had set out, Li Zhigang of the Ministry of Rites reported that Jin was discontent, and his assignment was changed to Jiaozhi, with orders to supervise grain supplies at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年，縉奏事入京，值帝北征，縉謁皇太子而還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle, Jin reported affairs and entered the capital; it happened the Emperor was on northern expedition—Jin paid respects to the Crown Prince and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Yongle reign, Jin came to the capital on official business while the Emperor was away on a northern campaign; he paid his respects to the Crown Prince and then returned.

sentences.zh: 漢王言縉伺上出，私覲太子，徑歸，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han said Jin waited for the Emperor to go out, privately visited the Crown Prince, directly returned—without a subject's rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han reported that Jin had waited until the Emperor was away, paid a private visit to the Crown Prince, and then left without observing proper court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 縉時方偕檢討王偁道廣東，覽山川，上疏請鑿贛江通南北。

translations.literal: Jin at that time was just then together with Compiler Wang Cheng touring Guangdong by road, viewing mountains and rivers; he submitted a memorial requesting to dredge the Gan River to connect north and south.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jin was traveling through Guangdong with Compiler Wang Cheng, surveying the landscape, and submitted a memorial proposing to dredge the Gan River to link north and south.

sentences.zh: 奏至，逮縉下詔獄，拷掠備至。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Jin was arrested and put in the imperial prison; torture was applied to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Jin was arrested and thrown into the imperial prison, where he was tortured without mercy.

sentences.zh: 詞連大理丞湯宗，宗人府經歷高得抃，中允李貫，贊善王汝玉，編修硃紘，檢討蔣驥、潘畿、蕭引高並及至剛，皆下獄。

translations.literal: Testimony implicated Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Tang Zong, Manager of the Imperial Clan Court Gao Debien, Palace Secretary Li Guan, Tutor Wang Ruyu, Compiler Zhu Hong, and Compilers Jiang Ji, Pan Ji, and Xiao Yingao, together with Li Zhigang—all were put in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation implicated Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Tang Zong, Manager of the Imperial Clan Court Gao Debien, Palace Secretary Li Guan, Tutor Wang Ruyu, Compiler Zhu Hong, Compilers Jiang Ji, Pan Ji, and Xiao Yingao, and Li Zhigang—all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 汝玉、貫、紘、引高、得抃皆瘐死。

translations.literal: Ruyu, Guan, Hong, Yingao, and Debien all died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruyu, Li Guan, Zhu Hong, Xiao Yingao, and Gao Debien all died in prison.

sentences.zh: 十三年，錦衣衛帥紀綱上囚籍，帝見縉姓名曰：「縉猶在耶？」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard Ji Gang submitted the prisoner register; the Emperor saw Jin's name and said: "Jin is still alive?
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, the commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, Ji Gang, submitted the prisoner register. The Emperor saw Jin's name and said, "Jin is still alive?

sentences.zh: 綱遂醉縉酒，埋積雪中，立死。

translations.literal: Gang then got Jin drunk on wine, buried him in accumulated snow, and he died immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Gang got Jin drunk, buried him in a snowdrift, and he died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 年四十七。

translations.literal: He was forty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-seven years old.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，妻子宗族徙遼東。

translations.literal: His household was confiscated; wife, children, and clan were banished to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His property was confiscated, and his wife, children, and entire clan were exiled to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 縉初與胡廣同侍成祖宴。

translations.literal: Jin had earlier attended a banquet together with Hu Guang in attendance on Emperor Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Jin and Hu Guang both attended a banquet in the service of Emperor Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾二人生同里，長同學，仕同官。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You two were born in the same home district, grew up as schoolmates, and hold the same office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You two were born in the same hometown, studied together as youths, and now serve in the same office.

sentences.zh: 縉有子，廣可以女妻之。」

translations.literal: Jin has a son; Guang may give him a daughter in marriage."
translations.idiomatic: Jin has a son—Guang may betroth his daughter to him."

sentences.zh: 廣頓首曰：「臣妻方娠，未卜男女。」

translations.literal: Guang kowtowed and said: "Your subject's wife is newly pregnant; it is not yet known whether the child will be male or female."
translations.idiomatic: Guang kowtowed and said, "Your subject's wife has just conceived, and we do not yet know whether the child will be a boy or a girl."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「定女矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "It will certainly be a girl."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled and said, "It will surely be a girl."

sentences.zh: 已而果生女，遂約婚。

translations.literal: Before long a daughter was indeed born, and they thereupon arranged the betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a daughter was indeed born, and the two families arranged the marriage.

sentences.zh: 縉敗，子禎亮徙遼東，廣欲離婚。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, his son Zhenliang was banished to Liaodong, and Guang wished to break off the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's downfall, his son Zhenliang was exiled to Liaodong, and Guang wanted to dissolve the betrothal.

sentences.zh: 女截耳誓曰：「薄命之婚，皇上主之，大人面承之，有死無二。」

translations.literal: The daughter cut off her ear and swore: "This ill-fated betrothal was ordained by the Emperor and accepted in person by my father; I shall die rather than take another."
translations.idiomatic: The daughter cut off her ear and vowed, "This fated marriage was ordained by the Emperor and accepted to his face by my father; I would rather die than marry anyone else."

sentences.zh: 及赦還，卒歸禎亮。

translations.literal: When an amnesty allowed them to return, she ultimately went to Zhenliang as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty permitted their return, she eventually went to Zhenliang and became his wife.

sentences.zh: 正統元年八月，詔還所籍家產。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhengtong, an edict restored their confiscated family property.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of the Zhengtong reign, an edict ordered the return of their confiscated family estate.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，復縉官，贈朝議大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, Jin's official rank was restored and he was posthumously given the title Grand Master of Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chenghua reign, Jin's official rank was restored, and he was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 始縉言漢王及安南事得禍。

translations.literal: From the first, Jin met disaster for speaking about the Prince of Han and the Annam affair.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset, Jin had brought disaster upon himself by speaking out about the Prince of Han and the Annam campaign.

sentences.zh: 後高煦以叛誅。

translations.literal: Later Gao Xu was executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Xu was put to death for treason.

sentences.zh: 安南數反，置吏未久，復棄去。

translations.literal: Annam rebelled repeatedly; officials were installed but not long afterward the territory was abandoned again.
translations.idiomatic: Annam rose in rebellion again and again; the court appointed officials there, but before long withdrew them and gave up the territory once more.

sentences.zh: 悉如縉言。

translations.literal: Everything happened just as Jin had said.
translations.idiomatic: Everything unfolded exactly as Jin had predicted.

sentences.zh: 縉兄綸，洪武中亦官御史。

translations.literal: Jin's elder brother Lun also served as a censor during the Hongwu period.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's elder brother Lun had also served as a censor in the Hongwu era.

sentences.zh: 性剛直。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature stern and upright.

sentences.zh: 後改應天教授。

translations.literal: He was later reassigned as professor at Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to serve as professor at Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 子禎期，以書名。

translations.literal: His son Zhenqi was renowned for calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhenqi won fame for his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 黃淮，字宗豫，永嘉人。

translations.literal: Huang Huai, styled Zongyu, was a native of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Huai, whose courtesy name was Zongyu, came from Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 父性，方國珍據溫州，遁跡避偽命。

translations.literal: His father Xing—when Fang Guozhen held Wenzhou—went into hiding to avoid serving the usurper's summons.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing had gone into hiding to avoid serving the rebel regime when Fang Guozhen held Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮舉洪武末進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: Huai passed the jinshi examination in late Hongwu and was appointed a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Huai passed the jinshi examination near the end of the Hongwu reign and was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，召對稱旨，命與解縉常立御榻左，備顧問。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu took the throne, Huai was summoned for audience and his replies pleased the Emperor, who ordered him to stand regularly to the left of the imperial couch together with Jie Jin, to be at hand for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzu acceded to the throne, Huai was summoned to audience and his answers pleased the Emperor, who ordered him to stand regularly at the left of the imperial couch with Jie Jin, ready to advise.

sentences.zh: 或至夜分，帝就寢，猶賜坐榻前語，機密重務悉預聞。

translations.literal: Sometimes until midnight—the Emperor would retire to sleep yet still grant him a seat before the couch to speak; he was privy to all confidential and weighty affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes discussions lasted until midnight; even after the Emperor retired to bed, he would still grant Huai a seat before the couch to talk, and Huai was privy to every confidential matter of state.

sentences.zh: 既而與縉等六人並直文淵閣，改翰林編修，進侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon he served in the Pavilion of Literary Depths together with Jin and five others, was transferred to Hanlin compiler, and promoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to the Pavilion of Literary Depths together with Jin and five others, transferred to Hanlin compiler, and promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 議立太子，淮請立嫡以長。

translations.literal: When they deliberated on establishing the Crown Prince, Huai urged that the eldest legitimate son be made heir.
translations.idiomatic: During deliberations over the installation of the Crown Prince, Huai argued that the eldest son of the principal consort should be named heir.

sentences.zh: 太子立，遷左庶子兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Once the Crown Prince was established, he was transferred to left tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: After the Crown Prince was installed, he was transferred to left tutor of the Heir Apparent while retaining his post as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年，解縉黜，淮進右春坊大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle, Jie Jin was demoted and Huai was promoted to grand secretary of the Right Chunfang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongle reign, Jie Jin was dismissed from office and Huai was promoted to grand secretary of the Right Chunfang.

sentences.zh: 明年與胡廣、金幼孜、楊榮、楊士奇同輔導太孫。

translations.literal: The next year he joined Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, Yang Rong, and Yang Shiqi in tutoring the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, Yang Rong, and Yang Shiqi in instructing the imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝北巡，命淮及蹇義、金忠、楊士奇輔皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Emperor toured the north, he ordered Huai together with Jian Yi, Jin Zhong, and Yang Shiqi to assist the Crown Prince in supervising the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Emperor made a northern tour, he ordered Huai, together with Jian Yi, Jin Zhong, and Yang Shiqi, to assist the Crown Prince in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 十一年，再北巡，仍留守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on a second northern tour, he remained behind as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the Emperor toured the north again, Huai remained behind to hold the capital as before.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝征瓦剌還，太子遣使迎稍緩，帝重入高煦譖，悉征東宮官屬下詔獄，淮及楊溥、金問皆坐系十年。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Emperor returned from campaigning against the Oirats, the Crown Prince's envoys to welcome him were somewhat slow; the Emperor again gave credence to Gao Xu's slanders, and all Eastern Palace officials were summoned and imprisoned in the imperial prison—Huai together with Yang Pu and Jin Wen were all convicted and detained for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Emperor returned from his campaign against the Oirats, the Crown Prince's welcoming envoys were somewhat delayed; the Emperor again believed Gao Xu's accusations, and all the Eastern Palace officials were summoned and thrown into the imperial prison—Huai, Yang Pu, and Jin Wen were all convicted and imprisoned for ten years.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，復官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, his offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, Huai's offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 尋擢為通政使，兼武英殿大學士，與楊榮、金幼孜、楊士奇同掌內製〔制〕。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to transmission commissioner, concurrently grand secretary of the Hall of Martial Brilliance, and together with Yang Rong, Jin Youzi, and Yang Shiqi oversaw the drafting of imperial compositions.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to transmission commissioner and concurrently appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Martial Brilliance, joining Yang Rong, Jin Youzi, and Yang Shiqi in overseeing the drafting of imperial compositions.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，乞終制。

translations.literal: Upon entering mourning for his mother, he requested to observe the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and he entered mourning, he asked to complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 明年，進少保、戶部尚書，兼大學士如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Junior Guardian and minister of revenue, while retaining his grand secretary post as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Junior Guardian and minister of revenue, while continuing to serve as grand secretary as before.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，太子在南京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong died, the Crown Prince was in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong died, the Crown Prince was in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 漢王久蓄異志，中外疑懼，淮憂危嘔血。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han had long harbored rebellious designs; within and without the court there was anxiety and fear, and Huai, gripped by worry, vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han had long nursed rebellious ambitions, and anxiety spread through court and country alike; Huai, consumed by dread, vomited blood.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，帝親征樂安，命淮居守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, when the Emperor personally marched against Le'an, he ordered Huai to remain and hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuande reign, when the Emperor personally led a campaign against Le'an, he ordered Huai to remain behind and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年以疾乞休，許之。

translations.literal: The next year, citing illness, he requested retirement, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to retire on grounds of illness, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 父性年九十，奉養甚歡。

translations.literal: His father Xing was ninety years old; Huai cared for him with great devotion and joy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing was ninety years old, and Huai supported him with devoted affection.

sentences.zh: 及性卒，賜葬祭，淮詣闕謝。

translations.literal: When Xing died, the court granted burial rites and sacrificial offerings; Huai came to the palace to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing died, the court granted funeral honors and sacrificial offerings, and Huai came to the palace to express his gratitude.

sentences.zh: 值燈時，賜游西苑，詔乘肩輿登萬歲山。

translations.literal: It happened to be Lantern Festival time; he was granted an outing to the Western Park and ordered to ride in a sedan chair up Longevity Hill.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be the Lantern Festival; he was granted an excursion to the Western Park and commanded to ride in a sedan chair up Longevity Hill.

sentences.zh: 命主會試，比辭歸，餞之太液池，帝為長歌送之，且曰：「朕生日，卿其復來。」

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed him chief examiner of the metropolitan examination; when he was about to take leave and return home, the Emperor feasted him at the Great Liquid Pool, composed a long song to send him off, and said: "On my birthday, you must come again."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed him chief examiner of the metropolitan examination; when he was about to take leave and return home, the Emperor gave him a farewell feast at the Great Liquid Pool, composed a long song to send him off, and said, "On my birthday, you must come again."

sentences.zh: 明年入賀。

translations.literal: The next year he came to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to offer birthday congratulations.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，再入朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he came to court again.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, he came to court once more.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年六月卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the fourteenth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 年八十三，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He was eighty-three years old; his posthumous title was Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-three years old; he was posthumously given the title Wenyuan, Literary and Simple.

sentences.zh: 淮性明果，達於治體。

translations.literal: Huai's nature was clear and resolute; he grasped the fundamentals of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was clear-minded and decisive, with a thorough grasp of the principles of government.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，長沙妖人李法良反。

translations.literal: During Yongle, the sorcerer Li Faliang of Changsha rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, the sorcerer Li Faliang of Changsha rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 仁宗方監國，命豐城侯李彬討之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was then supervising the realm and ordered Marquis Li Bin of Fengcheng to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was then supervising the realm and ordered Marquis Li Bin of Fengcheng to put down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 漢王忌太子有功，詭言彬不可用。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han, jealous of the Crown Prince's achievements, falsely claimed Bin was unfit for the task.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han, resentful of the Crown Prince's success, falsely claimed that Bin was unfit for the mission.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「彬，老將，必能滅賊，願急遣。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "Bin is a veteran general—he will surely destroy the bandits; I urge that he be dispatched at once."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "Bin is a seasoned general and will surely destroy the rebels; I urge that he be sent out immediately."

sentences.zh: 彬卒擒法良。

translations.literal: Bin ultimately captured Faliang.
translations.idiomatic: Bin ultimately captured Faliang.

sentences.zh: 又時有告黨逆者。

translations.literal: There were also at times accusers of cliques and treason.
translations.idiomatic: There were also periodic accusations of factional conspiracy and treason.

sentences.zh: 淮言於帝曰：「洪武末年已有敕禁，不宜復理。」

translations.literal: Huai said to the Emperor: "In the closing years of Hongwu there was already an edict forbidding this—it should not be pursued again."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said to the Emperor, "In the closing years of the Hongwu reign there was already an edict forbidding such prosecutions; they should not be revived."

sentences.zh: 吏部追論「靖難」兵起時，南人官北地不即歸附者，當編戍。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel pursued a prosecution holding that when the troops of the Jingnan campaign rose, southerners who held office in the north but did not promptly submit should be registered for penal service.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel proposed that southerners who had held office in the north but had not promptly submitted when the Jingnan campaign began should be registered for penal military service.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「如是，恐示人不廣。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "If it were done thus, I fear it would show the court as not magnanimous."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "If that were done, I fear it would show the court to be lacking in magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted all of these views.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted all of Huai's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台歸款，請得役屬吐蕃諸部。

translations.literal: Arughtai came in submission and requested to be allowed to levy and rule the various Tibetan tribes.
