translations.idiomatic: Arughtai submitted to the court and asked permission to levy and control the various Tibetan tribes.

sentences.zh: 求朝廷刻金作誓詞，磨其金酒中，飲諸酋長以盟。

translations.literal: He asked the court to inscribe an oath on gold, grind the gold into wine, and have the various chieftains drink it to seal the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to inscribe an oath on gold, grind the gold into wine, and have the chieftains drink it to seal the covenant.

sentences.zh: 眾議欲許之。

translations.literal: The assembled opinion was to grant the request.
translations.idiomatic: The consensus at court was to grant the request.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「彼勢分則易制，一則難圖矣。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "When their power is divided they are easy to control; if united, they will be hard to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "When their power is divided they are easy to control; once united, they will be hard to manage."

sentences.zh: 帝顧左右曰：「黃淮論事，如立高岡，無遠不見。」

translations.literal: The Emperor turned to those around him and said: "When Huang Huai discusses affairs, it is like standing on a high ridge—nothing far off escapes his view."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor turned to those beside him and said, "When Huang Huai discusses affairs, it is like standing on a high ridge—nothing distant escapes his sight."

sentences.zh: 西域僧大寶法王來朝，帝將刻玉印賜之，以璞示淮。

translations.literal: The Daba Fawang, a Buddhist monk from the western regions, came to court; the Emperor intended to have a jade seal carved and bestowed on him, and showed the raw jade to Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The Daba Fawang, a Buddhist monk from the western regions, came to court; the Emperor planned to have a jade seal carved and bestowed on him, and showed the uncut jade to Huai.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「朝廷賜諸番制敕，用『敕命』、『廣運』二寶。

translations.literal: Huai said: "When the court bestows edicts on the various frontier peoples, it uses the two seals 'Edict of Command' and 'Broadly Conveyed Fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "When the court bestows edicts on the frontier peoples, it uses the two imperial seals 'Edict of Command' and 'Broadly Conveyed Fortune.

sentences.zh: 今此玉較大，非所以示遠人、尊朝廷。」

translations.literal: This jade is larger than those—that is not the way to display dignity to distant peoples and honor the court."
translations.idiomatic: This piece of jade is larger than those seals; that is not the way to show dignity to distant peoples and honor the court."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his counsel and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 其獻替類如此。

translations.literal: His counsel in support of and opposition to proposals was largely of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel, whether in support of or in opposition to proposals, was largely of this sort.

sentences.zh: 然量頗隘。

translations.literal: Yet his magnanimity was rather narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his tolerance was rather limited.

sentences.zh: 同列有小過，輒以聞。

translations.literal: When colleagues had minor faults, he would immediately report them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a colleague committed a minor fault, he would immediately report it.

sentences.zh: 或謂解縉之謫，淮有力焉。

translations.literal: Some said Huai had a hand in Jie Jin's banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Huai had played a part in Jie Jin's banishment.

sentences.zh: 其見疏於宣宗也，亦謂楊榮言「淮病瘵，能染人」云。

translations.literal: When he fell from favor under Emperor Xuanzong, it was also said that Yang Rong had told the Emperor, "Huai suffers from consumption and can infect others."
translations.idiomatic: When he fell out of favor under Emperor Xuanzong, it was also said that Yang Rong had told the Emperor, "Huai suffers from consumption and can infect others."

sentences.zh: 時方討燕，廣對策有「親籓陸梁，人心搖動」語，帝親擢廣第一，賜名靖，授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: At the time the court was campaigning against Yan; in his examination response Guang included the phrase "a princely fief behaves insolently and people's hearts waver"; the Emperor personally ranked Guang first, granted him the name Jing, and appointed him Hanlin reviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was campaigning against Yan, Guang's examination essay contained the phrase "a princely fief grows unruly and the people's hearts are unsettled"; the Emperor personally ranked Guang first, granted him the name Jing, and appointed him Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，廣偕解縉迎附。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu took the throne, Guang together with Jie Jin came out to welcome and submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzu acceded to the throne, Guang went out together with Jie Jin to welcome and submit to him.

sentences.zh: 擢侍講，改侍讀，復名廣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to lecturer-in-waiting, then transferred to reader-in-waiting, and his name was restored to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to lecturer-in-waiting, then transferred to reader-in-waiting, and his name was restored to Guang.

sentences.zh: 遷右春坊右庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right tutor in the Right Chunfang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right tutor of the Right Chunfang.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年，進翰林學士，兼左春坊大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle he was promoted to Hanlin academician, concurrently grand secretary of the Left Chunfang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongle reign he was promoted to Hanlin academician and concurrently appointed grand secretary of the Left Chunfang.

sentences.zh: 帝北征，與楊榮、金幼孜從。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched north, he accompanied him together with Yang Rong and Jin Youzi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor marched north on campaign, Guang accompanied him together with Yang Rong and Jin Youzi.

sentences.zh: 數召對帳殿，或至夜分。

translations.literal: He was frequently summoned for audience in the campaign tent, sometimes until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: He was frequently summoned for audience in the campaign tent, sometimes until deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 過山川厄塞，立馬議論，行或稍後，輒遣騎四齣求索。

translations.literal: When they passed difficult terrain at mountain passes, they would dismount and discuss; if he fell somewhat behind on the march, the Emperor would dispatch horsemen in all directions to search for him.
translations.idiomatic: When they passed treacherous mountain terrain, they would dismount to discuss affairs; if Guang fell somewhat behind on the march, the Emperor would send horsemen in all directions to find him.

sentences.zh: 嘗失道，脫衣乘驏馬渡河，水沒馬及腰以上，帝顧勞良苦。

translations.literal: Once he lost his way, stripped off his clothes and crossed a river riding a mule; the water rose above the mule's waist, and the Emperor turned back to express sympathy for his hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Once he lost his way, stripped off his clothes, and crossed a river on a mule; the water rose above the mule's waist, and the Emperor turned back to express sympathy for his ordeal.

sentences.zh: 廣善書，每勒石，皆命書之。

translations.literal: Guang excelled at calligraphy; whenever steles were engraved, the Emperor ordered him to write the inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Guang excelled at calligraphy, and whenever a stele was to be engraved, the Emperor ordered him to write the inscription.

sentences.zh: 十二年再北征，皇長孫從，命廣與榮、幼孜軍中講經史。

translations.literal: On the second northern expedition in the twelfth year, when the eldest imperial grandson accompanied the campaign, the Emperor ordered Guang together with Rong and Youzi to lecture on the classics and history in the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the second northern expedition in the twelfth year, when the eldest imperial grandson accompanied the campaign, the Emperor ordered Guang, together with Rong and Youzi, to lecture on the classics and history in the army.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進文淵閣大學士，兼職如故。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to grand secretary of the Pavilion of Literary Depths, while retaining his other posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to grand secretary of the Pavilion of Literary Depths, while retaining his other offices as before.

sentences.zh: 帝征烏思藏僧作法會，為高帝、高後薦福，言見諸祥異。

translations.literal: The Emperor invited U-Tsang monks to perform Buddhist services to pray for blessings on the Grand Emperor and Grand Empress, and reports spoke of many auspicious marvels.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor invited monks from U-Tsang to perform Buddhist rites to pray for blessings on the founding emperor and empress, and reports spoke of many auspicious marvels.

sentences.zh: 廣乃獻《聖孝瑞應頌》，帝綴為佛曲，令宮中歌舞之。

translations.literal: Guang then presented "An Ode to Sacred Filiality and Auspicious Responses"; the Emperor arranged it into a Buddhist song and had it sung and danced in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guang then presented "An Ode to Sacred Filiality and Auspicious Responses"; the Emperor arranged it into a Buddhist hymn and had it sung and danced in the palace.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中周訥請封禪，廣言其不可，遂不許。

translations.literal: Zhou Ne, a department director of the Ministry of Rites, petitioned for a fengshan sacrifice; Guang said it was inadvisable, and the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ne, a department director in the Ministry of Rites, petitioned for a fengshan sacrifice; Guang argued against it, and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 廣上《卻封禪頌》，帝益親愛之。

translations.literal: Guang submitted "An Ode Declining the Fengshan"; the Emperor grew even fonder of him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted "An Ode Declining the Fengshan," and the Emperor grew even fonder of him.

sentences.zh: 廣性縝密。

translations.literal: Guang's nature was meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was meticulous by nature.

sentences.zh: 帝前所言及所治職務，出未嘗告人。

translations.literal: What he said before the Emperor and the official business he handled—once he left, he never told anyone.
translations.idiomatic: What he said before the Emperor and the official business he handled, he never disclosed to anyone once he left the palace.

sentences.zh: 時人以方漢胡廣。

translations.literal: People of the time likened him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time compared him to Hu Guang of the Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 然頗能持大體。

translations.literal: Yet he was quite able to uphold the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was quite capable of upholding the larger principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 奔母喪還朝，帝問百姓安否。

translations.literal: When he rushed home for his mother's funeral and returned to court, the Emperor asked whether the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court after rushing home for his mother's funeral, the Emperor asked whether the common people were living in peace.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安，但郡縣窮治建文時奸黨，株及支親，為民厲。」

translations.literal: He replied: "They are at peace, but counties and prefectures are exhaustively prosecuting the Jianwen-era factionalists, implicating collateral kin, and this is a scourge on the people."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "They are at peace, but counties and prefectures are exhaustively prosecuting the Jianwen-era factionalists, implicating collateral relatives, and this has become a scourge upon the people."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his statement.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the sixteenth year, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，諡文穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title minister of rites; his posthumous name was Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title minister of rites and given the posthumous name Wenmu, Literary and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 文臣得諡，自廣始。

translations.literal: Civil officials receiving posthumous titles began with Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of granting posthumous titles to civil officials began with Guang.

sentences.zh: 喪還，過南京，太子為致祭。

translations.literal: As the funeral procession returned, passing Nanjing, the Crown Prince offered sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral procession returned home, passing through Nanjing, the Crown Prince performed sacrificial rites in his honor.

sentences.zh: 明年，官其子穜翰林檢討。

translations.literal: The next year, his son Tong was given office as hanlin reviser.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, his son Tong was appointed a reviser in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，加贈廣少師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong acceded, Guang was additionally granted the posthumous title Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Guang was posthumously granted the title of Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 金幼孜

translations.literal: Jin Youzi
translations.idiomatic: Jin Youzi

sentences.zh: 金幼孜，名善，以字行，新淦人。

translations.literal: Jin Youzi, given name Shan, was known by his courtesy name, a native of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Youzi, whose given name was Shan but who was known by his courtesy name, came from Xingan.

sentences.zh: 建文二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the second year of the Jianwen reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed supervising secretary of the household section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，改翰林檢討，與解縉等同直文淵閣，遷侍講。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu came to the throne, he was changed to hanlin reviser, together with Jie Jin and others served at the Pavilion of Literary Depths, and was promoted to lecturing attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzu took the throne, he became a reviser in the Hanlin Academy and, together with Jie Jin and others, served in the Pavilion of Literary Depths; he was later promoted to lecturing attendant.

sentences.zh: 時翰林坊局臣講書東宮，皆先具經義，閣臣閱正，呈帝覽，乃進講。

translations.literal: At that time, members of the hanlin workshops who lectured on the classics in the Eastern Palace would first prepare the meaning of the text; cabinet ministers would review and correct it, present it for the Emperor's perusal, and only then proceed to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Hanlin scholars who lectured on the classics in the Eastern Palace would first draft their interpretations; cabinet ministers would review and revise them, submit them for the Emperor's approval, and only then proceed to the lectures.

sentences.zh: 解縉《書》，楊士奇《易》，胡廣《詩》，幼孜《春秋》，因進《春秋要旨》三卷。

translations.literal: Jie Jin on the Book of Documents, Yang Shiqi on the Book of Changes, Hu Guang on the Book of Poetry, and Youzi on the Spring and Autumn Annals; hence he submitted the Essential Points of the Spring and Autumn Annals in three fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Jin lectured on the Book of Documents, Yang Shiqi on the Book of Changes, Hu Guang on the Book of Poetry, and Youzi on the Spring and Autumn Annals; in this connection he submitted his Essential Points of the Spring and Autumn Annals in three fascicles.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年，遷右諭德兼侍講，因諭吏部，直內閣諸臣胡廣、金幼孜等考滿，勿改他任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle, he was transferred to right preceptor of the crown prince while also serving as lecturing attendant; the Emperor consequently instructed the ministry of personnel that the members of the inner cabinet such as Hu Guang and Jin Youzi, when their terms expired, were not to be transferred to other posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongle reign, he was promoted to right preceptor of the crown prince while retaining his post as lecturing attendant. The Emperor then instructed the Ministry of Personnel that cabinet members such as Hu Guang and Jin Youzi were not to be reassigned when their terms of service expired.

sentences.zh: 七年從幸北京。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he accompanied the imperial tour to Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he accompanied the Emperor on his visit to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 明年北征，幼孜與廣、榮扈行，駕駐清水源，有泉涌出。

translations.literal: The next year on the northern expedition, Youzi together with Guang and Rong escorted the tour; when the imperial carriage halted at Qingshuiyuan, a spring burst forth.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the northern expedition, Youzi accompanied Guang and Rong in escorting the Emperor. When the imperial procession halted at Clear Water Spring, a fresh spring burst from the ground.

sentences.zh: 幼孜獻銘，榮獻詩，皆勞以上尊。

translations.literal: Youzi presented an inscription, Rong presented a poem, and both were rewarded with superior wine.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi composed an inscription and Rong composed a poem, and both were rewarded with superior wine in recognition of their service.

sentences.zh: 帝重幼孜文學，所過山川要害，輒命記之。

translations.literal: The Emperor valued Youzi's literary learning; wherever they passed through mountains and rivers at strategic points, he would order them recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor valued Youzi's literary talent and, wherever the campaign passed strategic mountains and rivers, would order him to compose a record.

sentences.zh: 幼孜據鞍起草立就。

translations.literal: Youzi, leaning on the saddle, would draft compositions and finish them immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi would draft compositions from horseback and finish them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 使自瓦剌來，帝召幼孜等傍輿行，言敵中事，親倚甚。

translations.literal: When envoys came from Oirat, the Emperor summoned Youzi and others to walk beside the carriage and speak of affairs among the enemy; he relied on them with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys arrived from Oirat, the Emperor would summon Youzi and others to walk beside his carriage and discuss intelligence from the enemy camps; he relied on them with great intimacy.

sentences.zh: 嘗與廣、榮及侍郎金純失道陷谷中。

translations.literal: Once he, together with Guang, Rong, and vice minister Jin Chun, lost the way and fell into a ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Once he, together with Guang, Rong, and Vice Minister Jin Chun, lost their way and became trapped in a ravine.

sentences.zh: 暮夜，幼孜墜馬，廣、純去不顧。

translations.literal: At nightfall, Youzi fell from his horse; Guang and Chun went on without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall Youzi fell from his horse, while Guang and Chun rode on without stopping.

sentences.zh: 榮為結鞍行，行又輒墜，榮乘以己騎，明日始達行在所。

translations.literal: Rong secured the saddle and helped him walk; walking he again fell repeatedly; Rong gave him his own mount, and only on the morrow did they reach the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Rong fixed the saddle and helped him along on foot; when Youzi kept falling, Rong gave him his own horse. They did not reach the imperial camp until the following day.

sentences.zh: 是夜，帝遣使十余輩跡榮、幼孜，不獲。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor sent more than ten envoys to track Rong and Youzi, but they were not found.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Emperor dispatched more than ten messengers to search for Rong and Youzi, but they could not be found.

sentences.zh: 比至，帝喜動顏色。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the Emperor's joy showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: When they finally arrived, the Emperor's joy was written plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 自後北征皆從，所撰有北征前、後二《錄》。

translations.literal: From then on he accompanied every northern expedition; among his writings were two records of the northern campaign, one before and one after.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he accompanied every northern expedition. Among his writings are two Records of the Northern Campaign, one covering the period before and one the period after.

sentences.zh: 十二年命與廣、榮等纂《五經四書性理大全》，遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was ordered together with Guang, Rong, and others to compile the Great Compendium on the Nature and Principle of the Five Classics and Four Books; he was promoted to hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was ordered to compile, together with Guang, Rong, and others, the Great Compendium on the Nature and Principle of the Five Classics and Four Books, and was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 十八年與榮併進文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he and Rong were jointly promoted to grand secretaries of the Pavilion of Literary Depths.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he and Rong were jointly promoted to grand secretaries of the Pavilion of Literary Depths.

sentences.zh: 二十二年從北征，中道兵疲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he accompanied the northern expedition; midway the troops grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he accompanied the northern expedition, but midway the army grew exhausted.

sentences.zh: 帝以問群臣，莫敢對，惟幼孜言不宜深入，不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the assembled ministers; none dared reply; only Youzi said they ought not press deeper, but the Emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked his ministers; none dared answer. Only Youzi said they should not press deeper, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 次開平，帝謂榮、幼孜曰：「朕夢神人語上帝好生者再，是何祥也？」

translations.literal: When they reached Kaiping, the Emperor said to Rong and Youzi: "I dreamed a divine being say twice that God loves life—what omen is this?"
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Kaiping, the Emperor said to Rong and Youzi, "I dreamed that a divine being twice said that the Lord on High loves life—what omen is this?"

sentences.zh: 榮、幼孜對曰：「陛下此舉，固在除暴安民。

translations.literal: Rong and Youzi replied: "Your Majesty's present campaign is indeed meant to remove the violent and pacify the people.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Youzi replied, "Your Majesty's present campaign is indeed meant to suppress the violent and bring peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 然火炎昆岡，玉石俱毀，惟陛下留意。」

translations.literal: Yet when fire blazes on Mount Kun, jade and stone are destroyed together; may Your Majesty take heed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when fire blazes on Mount Kun, jade and common stone are destroyed alike—may Your Majesty take heed."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，即命草詔，招諭諸部。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved; he immediately ordered a draft edict to summon and declare to the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and immediately ordered a proclamation drafted to summon and reassure the various tribes.

sentences.zh: 還軍至榆木川，帝崩。

translations.literal: On the return march they reached Yumu Chuan; the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, when the army reached Elm River, the Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪。

translations.literal: The death was kept secret and the mourning not announced.
translations.idiomatic: The death was kept secret and mourning was not publicly announced.

sentences.zh: 榮訃京師，幼孜護梓宮歸。

translations.literal: Rong announced the death in the capital; Youzi escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Rong rode ahead to announce the death in the capital, while Youzi escorted the imperial coffin home.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，拜戶部右侍郎兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong came to the throne, he was appointed right vice minister of revenue, concurrently grand secretary of the Pavilion of Literary Depths.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was appointed right vice minister of revenue and grand secretary of the Pavilion of Literary Depths.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少保兼武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made junior guardian of the crown prince and grand secretary of the Hall of Martial Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed junior guardian of the crown prince and grand secretary of the Hall of Martial Glory.

sentences.zh: 是年十月命幼孜、榮、士奇會錄罪囚於承天門外。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, Youzi, Rong, and Shiqi were ordered jointly to review criminal cases outside the Gate of Receiving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That October, Youzi, Rong, and Shiqi were ordered to jointly review criminal cases outside the Gate of Receiving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 詔法司，錄重囚必會三學士，委寄益隆。

translations.literal: An edict to the judiciary declared that reviewing serious prisoners must convene the three grand secretaries; their trust and commission grew ever weightier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the judiciary declared that reviews of serious criminal cases must include the three grand secretaries, and their trust and authority grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 帝御西角門閱廷臣制誥，顧三學士曰：「汝三人及蹇、夏二尚書，皆先帝舊臣，朕方倚以自輔。

translations.literal: The Emperor attended the West Corner Gate to review the appointments and edicts of court ministers, turned to the three grand secretaries and said: "You three, together with the two ministers Jian and Xia, are all former ministers of the late Emperor; I am now relying on you to assist me.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing court appointments and edicts at the West Corner Gate, the Emperor turned to the three grand secretaries and said, "You three, together with Ministers Jian and Xia, are all former ministers of the late Emperor. I mean to rely on you to assist me.

sentences.zh: 嘗見前代人主惡聞直言，雖素所親信，亦畏威順旨，緘默取容。

translations.literal: I have seen that rulers of previous ages hated to hear frank speech; even those they had long trusted would fear their authority and follow their wishes, keeping silent to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen that rulers of earlier ages hated to hear frank counsel. Even those they had long trusted would fear their authority, defer to their wishes, and keep silent to win favor.

sentences.zh: 賢良之臣，言不見聽，退而杜口。

translations.literal: Worthy ministers whose words went unheeded would withdraw and seal their lips.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy ministers whose counsel went unheeded would withdraw and seal their lips.

sentences.zh: 朕與卿等當深用為戒。」

translations.literal: You and I must take this deeply as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: You and I must take this deeply to heart as a warning."

sentences.zh: 因取五人誥詞，親增二語云：「勿謂崇高而難入，勿以有所從違而或怠。」

translations.literal: He then took the five men's appointment edicts and personally added two lines: "Do not suppose that because one is lofty it is hard to approach; do not because one sometimes agrees or disagrees grow slack."
translations.idiomatic: He then took the five men's appointment edicts and personally added two lines: "Do not suppose that because one stands in high station it is hard to gain access; do not slacken because one sometimes agrees or disagrees."

sentences.zh: 幼孜等頓首稱謝。

translations.literal: Youzi and the others bowed their heads in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi and the others bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年進禮部尚書兼大學士、學士如故，並給三俸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he was promoted to minister of rites, concurrently grand secretary; his title of academician remained as before, and he was granted three salaries altogether.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Hongxi reign he was promoted to minister of rites and retained his post as grand secretary; his Hanlin title remained unchanged, and he was granted three salaries in total.

sentences.zh: 尋乞歸省母。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return home and visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he requested leave to return home and visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 明年，母卒。

translations.literal: The next year his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his mother died.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，詔起復，修兩朝實錄，充總裁官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, an edict recalled him to service; he compiled the Veritable Records of the two reigns and served as chief editor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, an edict recalled him to service. He compiled the Veritable Records of the two preceding reigns and served as chief editor.

sentences.zh: 三年持節寧夏，冊慶府郡王妃。

translations.literal: In the third year, bearing the imperial insignia, he went to Ningxia to invest the consort of the prince of the Qing fief as princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he traveled to Ningxia bearing the imperial insignia to invest the consort of the Prince of Qing as princess consort.

sentences.zh: 所過詢兵民疾苦，還奏之。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed he inquired into the hardships of troops and civilians, and on his return he memorialized them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he passed he inquired into the hardships of soldiers and civilians and reported them upon his return.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted his report.

sentences.zh: 從巡邊，度雞鳴山。

translations.literal: He accompanied the border tour and crossed Cockcrow Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the border inspection and crossed Cockcrow Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「唐太宗恃其英武征遼，嘗過此山。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Emperor Taizong of Tang, relying on his martial prowess, campaigned against Liaodong and once passed this mountain."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Emperor Taizong of Tang, trusting in his martial prowess, once campaigned against Liaodong and passed this mountain."

sentences.zh: 幼孜對曰：「太宗尋悔此役，故建憫忠閣。」

translations.literal: Youzi replied: "Taizong soon regretted that campaign, and for that reason built the Pavilion of Pity for the Loyal."
translations.idiomatic: Youzi replied, "Taizong soon regretted that campaign, which is why he built the Pavilion of Pity for the Loyal."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此山崩於元順帝時，為元亡征。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This mountain collapsed in the time of Emperor Shundi of Yuan—a portent of the Yuan's fall."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "This mountain collapsed during the reign of Emperor Shundi of Yuan—a portent of the dynasty's fall."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「順帝亡國之主，雖山不崩，國亦必亡。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Shundi was a ruler who lost his state; even if the mountain had not collapsed, the state would still have perished."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Shundi was a ruler who lost his empire. Even if the mountain had not collapsed, the state would still have fallen."

sentences.zh: 宣德六年十二月卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Xuande he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the sixth year of the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 年六十四。

translations.literal: He was sixty-four years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，諡文靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian; his posthumous name was Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian and given the posthumous name Wenjing, Literary and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 幼孜簡易靜默，寬裕有容。

translations.literal: Youzi was plain and undemanding, quiet and taciturn, generous and forbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi was plain and unassuming, quiet by nature, generous, and forbearing.

sentences.zh: 眷遇雖隆，而自處益謙。

translations.literal: Though imperial favor was great, he conducted himself with ever greater humility.
translations.idiomatic: Though imperial favor ran deep, he conducted himself with ever greater humility.

sentences.zh: 名其宴居之室曰「退庵」。

translations.literal: He named his chamber for leisure and repose the "Retreat Hermitage."
translations.idiomatic: He named his private study the "Hermitage of Withdrawal."

sentences.zh: 疾革時，家人囑請身後恩，不聽，曰：「此君子所恥也。」

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical, his family urged him to request posthumous honors; he would not listen and said: "This is what a gentleman would be ashamed of."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew critical, his family urged him to request posthumous honors, but he refused, saying, "That is something a gentleman ought to be ashamed to do."

sentences.zh: 胡儼，字若思，南昌人。

translations.literal: Hu Yan, styled Ruosi, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yan, whose courtesy name was Ruosi, came from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 少嗜學，於天文、地理、律歷、醫卜無不究覽。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; in astronomy, geography, calendrics, medicine, and divination there was none he did not thoroughly study.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and thoroughly explored astronomy, geography, calendrics, medicine, and divination.

sentences.zh: 洪武中以舉人授華亭教諭，能以師道自任。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign, as a presented scholar he was appointed instructor at Huating and was able to take upon himself the way of the teacher.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he was appointed instructor at Huating as a presented scholar and took upon himself the full dignity of a teacher.

sentences.zh: 母憂，服除，改長垣，乞便地就養，復改余干。

translations.literal: After mourning for his mother, when the mourning period ended, he was transferred to Changyuan; he requested a convenient post to support his parents and was again transferred to Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he was transferred to Changyuan. He then requested a more convenient post so he could support his parents and was reassigned to Yugan.

sentences.zh: 學官許乞便地自儼始。

translations.literal: The permission for educational officials to request convenient posts began with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Educational officials' permission to request convenient posts for family care began with Yan.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，曰：「儼知天文，其令欽天監試。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu came to the throne, he said: "Yan knows astronomy—have the Directorate of Astronomy test him."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzu took the throne, he said, "Yan knows astronomy—have the Directorate of Astronomy test him."

sentences.zh: 既試，奏儼實通象緯、氣候之學。

translations.literal: After the test, a memorial reported that Yan was truly versed in the learning of astral signs and seasonal phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: After the test, a memorial reported that Yan was genuinely versed in astral lore and seasonal forecasting.

sentences.zh: 尋又以解縉薦，授翰林檢討，與縉等俱直文淵閣，遷侍講，進左庶子。

translations.literal: Soon, recommended by Jie Jin, he was appointed hanlin reviser; together with Jin and others he served at the Pavilion of Literary Depths, was promoted to lecturing attendant, and advanced to left assistant tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on Jie Jin's recommendation, he was appointed a reviser in the Hanlin Academy and, together with Jin and others, served in the Pavilion of Literary Depths. He was promoted to lecturing attendant and then to left assistant tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 父喪，起復。

translations.literal: When his father died, he was recalled from mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he was recalled from mourning to resume office.

sentences.zh: 儼在閣，承顧問，嘗不欲先人，然少戇。

translations.literal: Yan in the cabinet received imperial consultation; he was always unwilling to speak before others, yet he was somewhat blunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the cabinet Yan answered the Emperor's consultations. He was always reluctant to speak before others, yet he could be somewhat blunt.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年九月，拜國子監祭酒，遂不預機務。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Yongle, he was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education and from then on did not participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of the Yongle reign he was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education and thereafter ceased to participate in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 時用法嚴峻，國子生托事告歸者坐戍邊。

translations.literal: At that time the law was applied severely; students of the imperial academy who secured leave on pretext were punished with frontier garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: At that time penalties were harsh: students who obtained leave on pretext were sentenced to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 儼至，即奏除之。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived, he immediately memorialized to abolish this.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Yan took office, he memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝幸北京，召儼赴行在。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Emperor visited Beijing and summoned Yan to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Emperor visited Beijing and summoned Yan to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 明年北征，命以祭酒兼侍講，掌翰林院事，輔皇太孫留守北京。

translations.literal: The next year on the northern expedition, he was ordered as chancellor while also serving as lecturing attendant to manage the affairs of the Hanlin Academy and assist the imperial grandson in remaining to guard Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, during the northern expedition, he was ordered to serve as chancellor while also holding the post of lecturing attendant, to manage the Hanlin Academy and assist the imperial grandson in governing Beijing in the Emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 十九年，改北京國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to chancellor of the Beijing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became chancellor of the Beijing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 當是時，海內混一，垂五十年。

translations.literal: At that time, within the seas all was unified, nearly fifty years having passed.
translations.idiomatic: By then the empire had been unified for nearly fifty years.

sentences.zh: 帝方內興禮樂，外懷要荒，公卿大夫彬彬多文學之士。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then promoting rites and music within and cherishing the distant frontiers without; among grandees and ministers many were men of refined literary attainment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was promoting rites and music at home while reaching out to distant frontiers abroad, and among grandees and ministers there were many men of refined literary culture.

sentences.zh: 儼館閣宿儒，朝廷大著作多出其手，重修《太祖實錄》、《永樂大典》、《天下圖志》皆充總裁官。

translations.literal: Yan was a seasoned scholar of the academies; many of the court's great compilations came from his hand—he served as chief editor of the Revised Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor, the Yongle Encyclopedia, and the Universal Geographical Atlas.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was a seasoned scholar of the academies, and many of the court's major compilations came from his hand. He served as chief editor of the Revised Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor, the Yongle Encyclopedia, and the Universal Geographical Atlas.

sentences.zh: 居國學二十餘年，以身率教，動有師法。

translations.literal: He dwelt in charge of the imperial academy for more than twenty years, personally setting the standard of instruction; in every action he embodied the teacher's method.
translations.idiomatic: He led the imperial academy for more than twenty years, personally setting the standard of instruction and embodying the teacher's discipline in every action.

sentences.zh: 洪熙改元，以疾乞休，仁宗賜敕獎勞，進太子賓客，仍兼祭酒。

translations.literal: When the Hongxi reign era was declared, he requested retirement on grounds of illness; Emperor Renzong granted an edict of commendation and reward, promoted him to mentor of the crown prince, while he still concurrently held the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongxi reign era began, he requested retirement due to illness. Emperor Renzong granted him a commendatory edict, promoted him to mentor of the crown prince, and let him retain the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 致仕，復其子孫。

translations.literal: Upon retirement, his descendants were restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his retirement, his descendants were restored to office.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，以禮部侍郎召，辭歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he was summoned as vice minister of rites, but he declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, he was summoned as vice minister of rites, but he declined and returned home.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，方岳重臣咸待以師禮。

translations.literal: He lived at home for twenty years; provincial governors and great ministers all treated him with the respect due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for twenty years, and provincial governors and senior ministers all treated him with the respect due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 儼與言，未嘗及私。

translations.literal: When Yan spoke with them, he never touched on private matters.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation Yan never touched on private matters.

sentences.zh: 自處淡泊，歲時衣食才給。

translations.literal: He conducted himself in simplicity and detachment; from year to year his food and clothing barely sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply and quietly, with barely enough food and clothing from year to year.

sentences.zh: 初為湖廣考官，得楊溥文，大異之，題其上曰：「必能為董子之正言，而不為公孫之阿曲。」

translations.literal: Early on as examiner in Huguang, he obtained Yang Pu's essay and was greatly struck by it; he inscribed on it: "He will surely be able to speak the upright words of Dong Zhongshu and not the flattering crookedness of Gongsun Hong."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, as an examiner in Huguang, he came upon Yang Pu's examination essay and was deeply impressed. He wrote on it, "He will surely speak the upright words of Dong Zhongshu, and not the flattering crookedness of Gongsun Hong."

sentences.zh: 世以為知人。

translations.literal: The world regarded this as proof that he knew men.
translations.idiomatic: People took this as proof of his gift for recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 正統八年八月卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year of Zhengtong he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the eighth year of the Zhengtong reign, at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明初罷丞相，分事權於六部。

translations.literal: The encomium says: At the beginning of Ming the office of chancellor was abolished and governmental authority was divided among the six ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: At the founding of the Ming dynasty the office of chancellor was abolished and governmental authority was divided among the six ministries.

sentences.zh: 成祖始命儒臣直文淵閣，預機務。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu first ordered Confucian officials to serve at the Pavilion of Literary Depths and participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu was the first to order Confucian officials to serve in the Pavilion of Literary Depths and participate in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 沿及仁、宣，而閣權日重，實行丞相事。

translations.literal: Extending through the Ren and Xuan reigns, cabinet authority grew daily heavier and in effect performed the chancellor's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Through the reigns of Renzong and Xuanzong, cabinet authority grew ever weightier until it in effect performed the duties of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 解縉以下五人，則詞林之最初入閣者也。

translations.literal: The five men from Jie Jin downward were the first from the literary academy to enter the cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Jin and the four men who followed him were the first literary academicians to enter the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 夫處禁密之地，必以公正自持，而尤貴於厚重不泄。

translations.literal: For one who occupies a secluded and confidential post, he must uphold himself with impartiality and rectitude, and above all value solidity and discretion and not divulge secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Those who occupy such secluded and confidential posts must uphold themselves with impartiality and rectitude, and above all must value discretion and the refusal to divulge secrets.

sentences.zh: 縉少年高才，自負匡濟大略，太祖俾十年進學，愛之深矣。

translations.literal: Jin in his youth was highly talented; he counted on himself great schemes for saving the realm; the founding Emperor had allowed him ten years to advance in learning and loved him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was a brilliant youth who trusted in his own grand schemes for saving the realm. The founding Emperor had granted him ten years to advance in learning and loved him deeply.

sentences.zh: 彼其動輒得謗，不克令終，夫豈盡嫉賢害能者力固使之然歟。

translations.literal: That he repeatedly earned slander and could not finish well—was it entirely the work of those jealous of worth and harmers of talent that made it so?
translations.idiomatic: That he repeatedly earned slander and could not finish well—is it entirely the work of those who envied talent and sought to destroy the able?

sentences.zh: 黃淮功在輔導，胡廣、金幼孜勞著扈從，胡儼久於國學。

translations.literal: Huang Huai's merit lay in instruction and guidance; Hu Guang and Jin Youzi distinguished themselves in escorting the imperial tours; Hu Yan served long in the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Huai's merit lay in instructing the heir; Hu Guang and Jin Youzi distinguished themselves in escorting the Emperor on campaign; Hu Yan served long as head of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 觀諸臣從容密勿，隨事納忠，固非僅以文字翰墨為勛績已也。

translations.literal: Observing these ministers—calm and confidentially diligent, offering loyalty as affairs arose—their achievement was certainly not merely in literary brushwork and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Observing how these ministers conducted themselves with calm discretion in confidential affairs, offering loyal counsel on every issue, it is clear that their merit lay in far more than literary composition alone.
